one_month_reasoning: No Jabil earnings in the window (Q1 FY27 report is expected mid-December 2026). The FY26 print on Sep 30 is already out: a beat with FY27 guidance above consensus ($17.55 vs ~$16.92), yet the stock fell 10% that day to $286.86 and then recovered 6% over two sessions to $304.41, so the post-print move has been partly reversed. Scheduled events inside the window: hyperscaler September-quarter earnings and 2027 capex commentary (roughly Oct 27-30), which is the main swing factor for AI-exposed EMS names; the late-October FOMC, where Polymarket prices further hikes in 2026 (a headwind to multiples); and macro and tariff headlines. Post-earnings drift after a positive fundamental surprise argues for a slight upward tilt, while the negative price reaction argues the other way, so I treat these as offsetting. The ladder is close to a symmetric lognormal around ~$305 with monthly volatility of about 13.4% (47%/3.5), with a slightly fatter left tail for the risk of a disappointing capex read-through.

FY27 lands below the $17.55 guide, FY28 EPS flattens near $16, and the multiple falls back to the historical 11x, as in past EMS down-cycles (2001, 2008).

base.story: Jabil delivers about the FY27 guide (revenue $44.5B, 6.1% core margin, $17.55 EPS). In late Sep-2027 it guides FY28 to roughly $20 EPS with growth slowing to mid-teens, and the stock holds ~15-16x NTM, close to today's price plus EPS growth less some multiple compression.

bull.story: Hyperscaler capex again beats consensus (as in 2024-25, when it grew 50%+ against ~20% expected). Jabil beats and raises through FY27, FY28 EPS reaches about $22, and the multiple re-rates toward 20x, near the June-2026 peak of $429.

thesis_break_reason: $215 is about 12x FY27 guided core EPS, back to the pre-AI historical multiple, and about 30% below today, beyond a 1-sigma monthly move. At that level the market would be pricing cuts to the FY27 guide (AI or cloud program losses, order push-outs, margin squeeze at a 6% core margin) or a cyclical EMS downturn, not ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Anchors: the FY27 guide ($44.5B revenue, $17.55 core EPS, ~$1.6B FCF; filing) puts the stock at ~17.3x forward. Historically Jabil traded at 11-14x (Sure Dividend; TIKR 5-yr ~14x), and it re-rated in 2025-26 on AI and cloud exposure. By the horizon the market will price FY28 (~$20 EPS by my estimate), so fair value is ~$309, close to spot: EPS growth roughly offsets an expected partial de-rating. Base rates: realized vol is 47%, and the stock traded $190-429 over the year with a ~30% drawdown from the June peak, so a wide distribution is warranted. EMS names have a record of sharp de-ratings when end-market capex turns (2001, 2008), which fattens the left tail. Prediction markets show low near-term recession odds (7.5% by end-2026, $2.2M volume) but higher odds by end-2027 (34.5%, very thin), and 17.5% for an 'AI bubble burst' by Jun-2027. Polymarket also prices Fed hikes, a headwind for multiples. Capex trackers (MS +29% in 2027, Moody's ~$1T) support continued demand, and consensus has underestimated capex two years running, which supports the bull tail. The 12-month ladder is a lognormal with median ~$308 and sigma ~0.43, slightly below realized vol because the business is diversified and has guidance visibility, with fattened left-tail mass for a cyclical bust. Scenario expected value is ~$311. The supervisor should note the stock fell 10% on a beat-and-raise: positioning is crowded and the market doubts margin and FCF conversion.
